name: Mike Lee

issue_poll.name: Deseret News/Hinckley Institute poll (Dan Jones & Associates), Sept 3–21, 2022
issue_poll.note: Most important issue for choosing a senator; ranks 3–5 tied at 9%, ranks 6–9 listed without percentages. Poll offered only 9 issues, so rank 10 is the next-highest issue in Pew's national Oct 2022 survey (future of democracy, 70% very important): https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2022/11/03/key-facts-about-u-s-voter-priorities-ahead-of-the-2022-midterm-elections/

issues.position: Oppose large federal spending bills, including his own party's

votes.question: On the motion to concur in the House amendment

issues.note: Opposed the 2024 funding package; backed the 2025 Republican full-year funding bill.

issues.position: Let cities acquire nearby federal land for housing
issues.note: No floor vote; his 2025 land-sale provision was pulled from H.R.1 before a vote.

issues.position: Allow drug imports instead of government price negotiation
issues.note: No Senate floor vote on drug importation or repealing Medicare negotiation this term.

issues.position: End federal student loan programs; oppose loan forgiveness

votes.bill_title: Disapproval of student loan debt cancellation
votes.question: On passage

issues.position: Speed permits for water storage (Unshackled Act)
issues.note: No Senate floor vote on water-storage permitting reform this term.

issues.position: Leave abortion to states; oppose a national ban

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: No national-ban vote held; rated on opposing a federal abortion-rights law.

issues.position: Roll back existing gun control laws

votes.bill_title: Disapproval of ATF pistol stabilizing brace rule
votes.question: On passage

issues.position: Fund border wall; restrict asylum and Flores release rules
issues.note: H.R.1 funded border wall construction; asylum and Flores changes got no floor vote.

issues.position: Keep the Court at nine justices; oppose court packing
issues.note: No floor vote on Court size this term.

issues.position: Called 2020 election fair; said confidence should be restored

caveats: Economy rated on two appropriations votes; the 2025 Yea on a $1.7T Republican funding bill is judged inconsistent with his pledge to oppose large spending even from his own party.
Pistol-brace roll call 171 inferred from usquery/thenewamerican vote IDs; S.4554 (211) and H.R.1 (372) numbers taken from the worked example, not confirmed independently for Lee.
Rank 10 comes from national Pew polling because the Utah poll listed only nine issues.
